description: Allows for the management of Lambda functions.

parameters.name: access_key
parameters.description: AWS access key ID. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID or AWS_ACCESS_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The aws_access_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_access_key_id alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: architecture
parameters.description: The instruction set architecture that the function supports. Requires one of s3_bucket or zip_file. Choices: "x86_64" "arm64"

parameters.name: aws_ca_bundle
parameters.description: The location of a CA Bundle to use when validating SSL certificates. The AWS_CA_BUNDLE environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: aws_config
parameters.description: A dictionary to modify the botocore configuration. Parameters can be found in the AWS documentation https://botocore.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/reference/config.html#botocore.config.Config.

parameters.name: dead_letter_arn
parameters.description: The parent object that contains the target Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an Amazon SQS queue or Amazon SNS topic.

parameters.name: debug_botocore_endpoint_logs
parameters.description: Use a botocore.endpoint logger to parse the unique (rather than total) "resource:action" API calls made during a task, outputing the set to the resource_actions key in the task results. Use the aws_resource_action callback to output to total list made during a playbook. The ANSIBLE_DEBUG_BOTOCORE_LOGS environment variable may also be used. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: A short, user-defined function description. Lambda does not use this value. Assign a meaningful description as you see fit. Default: ""

parameters.name: endpoint_url
parameters.description: URL to connect to instead of the default AWS endpoints. While this can be used to connection to other AWS-compatible services the amazon.aws and community.aws collections are only tested against AWS. The AWS_URL environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: environment_variables
parameters.description: A dictionary of environment variables the Lambda function is given.

parameters.name: handler
parameters.description: The function within your code that Lambda calls to begin execution.

parameters.name: image_uri
parameters.description: The Amazon ECR URI of the image to use. Required (alternative to runtime zip_file and s3_bucket) when creating a function. Required when state=present.

parameters.name: kms_key_arn
parameters.description: The KMS key ARN used to encrypt the function’s environment variables.

parameters.name: layers
parameters.description: A list of function layers to add to the function’s execution environment. Specify each layer by its ARN, including the version.

parameters.name: memory_size
parameters.description: The amount of memory, in MB, your Lambda function is given. Default: 128

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name you want to assign to the function you are uploading. Cannot be changed.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: A named AWS profile to use for authentication. See the AWS documentation for more information about named profiles https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-profiles.html. The AWS_PROFILE environment variable may also be used. The profile option is mutually exclusive with the aws_access_key, aws_secret_key and session_token options.

parameters.name: purge_tags
parameters.description: If purge_tags=true and tags is set, existing tags will be purged from the resource to match exactly what is defined by tags parameter. If the tags parameter is not set then tags will not be modified, even if purge_tags=True. Tag keys beginning with aws: are reserved by Amazon and can not be modified. As such they will be ignored for the purposes of the purge_tags parameter. See the Amazon documentation for more information https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws_tagging.html#tag-conventions. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The AWS region to use. For global services such as IAM, Route53 and CloudFront, region is ignored. The AWS_REGION environment variable may also be used. See the Amazon AWS documentation for more information http://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#ec2_region.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that Lambda assumes when it executes your function to access any other Amazon Web Services (AWS) resources. You may use the bare ARN if the role belongs to the same AWS account. Required when state=present.

parameters.name: runtime
parameters.description: The runtime environment for the Lambda function you are uploading. Required when creating a function. Uses parameters as described in boto3 docs. Required when state=present. For supported list of runtimes, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-runtimes.html.

parameters.name: s3_bucket
parameters.description: Amazon S3 bucket name where the .zip file containing your deployment package is stored. If state=present then either zip_file or s3_bucket must be present. s3_bucket and s3_key are required together.

parameters.name: s3_key
parameters.description: The Amazon S3 object (the deployment package) key name you want to upload. s3_bucket and s3_key are required together.

parameters.name: s3_object_version
parameters.description: The Amazon S3 object (the deployment package) version you want to upload.

parameters.name: secret_key
parameters.description: AWS secret access key. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY or AWS_SECRET_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The secret_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_secret_access_key alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: session_token
parameters.description: AWS STS session token for use with temporary credentials. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SESSION_TOKEN environment variable may also be used. The session_token and profile options are mutually exclusive.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Create or delete Lambda function. Choices: "present" ← (default) "absent"

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: A dictionary representing the tags to be applied to the resource. If the tags parameter is not set then tags will not be modified.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: The function maximum execution time in seconds after which Lambda should terminate the function. Default: 3

parameters.name: tracing_mode
parameters.description: Set mode to ‘Active’ to sample and trace incoming requests with AWS X-Ray. Turned off (set to ‘PassThrough’) by default. Choices: "Active" "PassThrough"

parameters.name: validate_certs
parameters.description: When set to false, SSL certificates will not be validated for communication with the AWS APIs. Setting validate_certs=false is strongly discouraged, as an alternative, consider setting aws_ca_bundle instead. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: vpc_security_group_ids
parameters.description: List of VPC security group IDs to associate with the Lambda function. Required when vpc_subnet_ids is used.

parameters.name: vpc_subnet_ids
parameters.description: List of subnet IDs to run Lambda function in. Use this option if you need to access resources in your VPC. Leave empty if you don’t want to run the function in a VPC. If set, vpc_security_group_ids must also be set.

parameters.name: zip_file
parameters.description: A .zip file containing your deployment package If state=present then either zip_file or s3_bucket must be present.

examples:
# Create Lambda functions
- name: looped creation
  amazon.aws.lambda:
    name: '{{ item.name }}'
    state: present
    zip_file: '{{ item.zip_file }}'
    runtime: 'python2.7'
    role: 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/lambda_basic_execution'
    handler: 'hello_python.my_handler'
    vpc_subnet_ids:
      - subnet-123abcde
      - subnet-edcba321
    vpc_security_group_ids:
      - sg-123abcde
      - sg-edcba321
    environment_variables: '{{ item.env_vars }}'
    tags:
      key1: 'value1'
  loop:
    - name: HelloWorld
      zip_file: hello-code.zip
      env_vars:
        key1: "first"
        key2: "second"
    - name: ByeBye
      zip_file: bye-code.zip
      env_vars:
        key1: "1"
        key2: "2"

# To remove previously added tags pass an empty dict
- name: remove tags
  amazon.aws.lambda:
    name: 'Lambda function'
    state: present
    zip_file: 'code.zip'
    runtime: 'python2.7'
    role: 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/lambda_basic_execution'
    handler: 'hello_python.my_handler'
    tags: {}

# Basic Lambda function deletion
- name: Delete Lambda functions HelloWorld and ByeBye
  amazon.aws.lambda:
    name: '{{ item }}'
    state: absent
  loop:
    - HelloWorld
    - ByeBye

# Create Lambda functions with function layers
- name: looped creation
  amazon.aws.lambda:
    name: 'HelloWorld'
    state: present
    zip_file: 'hello-code.zip'
    runtime: 'python2.7'
    role: 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/lambda_basic_execution'
    handler: 'hello_python.my_handler'
    layers:
      - layer_version_arn: 'arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:123456789012:layer:python27-env:7'

return_values.name: code
return_values.description: The lambda function’s code returned by get_function in boto3. Returned: success

return_values.name: location
return_values.description: The presigned URL you can use to download the function’s .zip file that you previously uploaded. The URL is valid for up to 10 minutes. Returned: success Sample: "https://prod-04-2014-tasks.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/snapshots/sample"

return_values.name: repository_type
return_values.description: The repository from which you can download the function. Returned: success Sample: "S3"

return_values.name: configuration
return_values.description: The Lambda function’s configuration metadata returned by get_function in boto3. Returned: success

return_values.name: architectures
return_values.description: The architectures supported by the function. Returned: success Sample: ["arm64"]

return_values.name: code_sha256
return_values.description: The SHA256 hash of the function’s deployment package. Returned: success Sample: "zOAGfF5JLFuzZoSNirUtOrQp+S341IOA3BcoXXoaIaU="

return_values.name: code_size
return_values.description: The size of the function’s deployment package in bytes. Returned: success Sample: 123

return_values.name: dead_letter_config
return_values.description: The function’s dead letter queue. Returned: when the function has a dead letter queue configured Sample: {"target_arn": "arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:123456789012:function:myFunction:1"}

return_values.name: target_arn
return_values.description: The ARN of an SQS queue or SNS topic. Returned: when the function has a dead letter queue configured Sample: "arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:123456789012:function:myFunction:1"

return_values.name: description
return_values.description: The function’s description. Returned: success Sample: "My function"

return_values.name: environment
return_values.description: The function’s environment variables. Returned: when environment variables exist

return_values.name: error
return_values.description: Error message for environment variables that could not be applied. Returned: when there is an error applying environment variables

return_values.name: error_code
return_values.description: The error code. Returned: when there is an error applying environment variables

return_values.name: message
return_values.description: The error message. Returned: when there is an error applying environment variables

return_values.name: variables
return_values.description: Environment variable key-value pairs. Returned: when environment variables exist Sample: {"key": "value"}

return_values.name: function_arn
return_values.description: The function’s Amazon Resource Name (ARN). Returned: on success Sample: "arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:123456789012:function:myFunction:1"

return_values.name: function_name
return_values.description: The function’s name. Returned: on success Sample: "myFunction"

return_values.name: handler
return_values.description: The function Lambda calls to begin executing your function. Returned: on success Sample: "index.handler"

return_values.name: last_modified
return_values.description: The date and time that the function was last updated, in ISO-8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssTZD). Returned: on success Sample: "2017-08-01T00:00:00.000+0000"

return_values.name: layers
return_values.description: The function’s layers. Returned: on success

return_values.name: arn
return_values.description: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the function layer. Returned: always Sample: "active"

return_values.name: signing_job_arn
return_values.description: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a signing job. Returned: always

return_values.name: signing_profile_version_arn
return_values.description: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for a signing profile version. Returned: always

return_values.name: memory_size
return_values.description: The memory allocated to the function. Returned: on success Sample: 128

return_values.name: revision_id
return_values.description: The latest updated revision of the function or alias. Returned: on success Sample: "a2x9886d-d48a-4a0c-ab64-82abc005x80c"

return_values.name: role
return_values.description: The function’s execution role. Returned: on success Sample: "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/lambda_basic_execution"

return_values.name: runtime
return_values.description: The funtime environment for the Lambda function. Returned: on success Sample: "nodejs6.10"

return_values.name: timeout
return_values.description: The amount of time that Lambda allows a function to run before terminating it. Returned: on success Sample: 3

return_values.name: tracing_config
return_values.description: The function’s AWS X-Ray tracing configuration. Returned: on success Sample: {"mode": "Active"}

return_values.name: mode
return_values.description: The tracing mode. Returned: on success Sample: "Active"

return_values.name: version
return_values.description: The version of the Lambda function. Returned: on success Sample: "1"

return_values.name: vpc_config
return_values.description: The function’s networking configuration. Returned: on success Sample: {"security_group_ids": [], "subnet_ids": [], "vpc_id": "123"}
